blocks.text: LOG:200–222 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

The Logic affordance block was reconsidered from first principles under the standing delegated authority. The review compared five genuinely different architectures per root, scored 45 candidates across 360 criterion values, routed 123 English concepts without forced atomization, passed all 18 canonical packet checks, passed all 24 complete Logic-family soundness checks, and passed the complete authority regression. All deterministic generated forms remained unchanged.

Approved architecture: LOG:2xx names substrate-neutral formal-evaluation affordances paired with canonical LOG:1xx evaluations. The inward triplet names one reference entity’s capacity for formal evaluation under its applicable internal criterion; the outward triplet names one specified constraint’s applicability to one distinct reference target; and the systemic triplet names capacity for one coordinated joint evaluation across multiple participants under one shared formal regime. The third trit changes only persistent, operative, or latent status.

LOG:200 — persistent internal formal evaluability — A persistent capacity of one reference entity to undergo formal evaluation under its applicable internal criterion, independently of whether that capacity is presently operative.
LOG:201 — operative internal formal evaluability — A capacity of one reference entity to undergo formal evaluation under its applicable internal criterion that is presently operative.
LOG:202 — latent internal formal evaluability — A capacity of one reference entity to undergo formal evaluation under its applicable internal criterion that exists without being presently operative.

LOG:210 — persistent constraint-target applicability — A persistent formal applicability relation between one specified constraint and one distinct reference target that can enable target constraint application, independently of whether that relation is presently operative.

LOG:211 — operative constraint-target applicability — A formal applicability relation between one specified constraint and one distinct reference target that presently enables target constraint application.

LOG:212 — latent constraint-target applicability — A formal applicability relation between one specified constraint and one distinct reference target that exists without presently enabling target constraint application.

LOG:220 — persistent systemic joint-evaluability — A persistent capacity of multiple participants under one shared formal regime to undergo one coordinated joint evaluation, independently of whether that capacity is presently operative.
LOG:221 — operative systemic joint-evaluability — A capacity of multiple participants under one shared formal regime to undergo one coordinated joint evaluation that is presently operative.

LOG:222 — latent systemic joint-evaluability — A capacity of multiple participants under one shared formal regime to undergo one coordinated joint evaluation that exists without being presently operative.

Design boundary: these roots do not silently encode the criterion or regime; actual evaluation; result polarity; technical decidability, computability, tractability, termination, or resource sufficiency; entailment, implication, consistency, compatibility, satisfiability, permission, authority, enforcement, data, algorithms, observer knowledge, scheduling, probability, or unrestricted modality. Inward evaluability requires no distinct target; outward applicability preserves one specified constraint and one distinct target; systemic joint-evaluability requires one coordinated evaluation under one shared regime. Persistent identity may co-occur with operative or latent status; operative and latent are mutually exclusive at one reference time. Lexical latency remains distinct from runtime [2]/num uncertainty.
